page: Amazon Web Services m9g.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and driven by the custom 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V3 processor. The configuration supplies 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache pool. System memory totals 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, requiring remote EBS volumes for persistent disk storage, while offering a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate competitive processing capability across both general integer and memory-dependent operations. The 48 physical cores achieve top-tier tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 624.06 GB/sec, Clang software compilation scores of 92,735.0, and overall multi-core Geekbench ratings of 28,111.0. Synthetic stress testing reveals strong multi-core performance alongside average single-core stress-ng results. In memory tests, the architecture exhibits high cached throughput alongside top-tier PassMark database operation rates and over 136 million Redis SET operations per second, while LLM inference throughput on small and medium models aligns within mid-tier averages.

The hardware configuration provides strong compute density and power-efficient processing typical of ARM architectures without the scheduling overhead of hyperthreaded cores. Because local storage is absent, architectures requiring high disk throughput must factor in networked storage dependency. Amazon Web Services m9g.12xlarge is well matched for large-scale microservice deployments, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, enterprise web application serving, continuous integration builds, and moderate relational database systems.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V3 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz and managed by the Nitro hypervisor. It integrates 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core, with 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance excludes bundled GPUs and local disks, relying fully on external network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compilation, compression, static web throughput, and in-memory key-value processing, alongside solid overall integer calculations. Its dedicated physical core architecture avoids hyperthreading contention, offering stable compute efficiency across varied cloud environments. The instance is suited for high-concurrency web serving, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD compilation pipelines, container fleets, and relational databases.
